R0024.title: Malicious Traffic Diversion
R0024.definition: Malicious traffic diversion through user-generated content refers to attackers tampering with, forging, or abusing user-generated content such as reviews and social shares to deceive users, redirect traffic, or achieve other malicious purposes.
R0024.description: Causes include: fake reviews and ratings to attract user clicks; social media abuse by fabricating fake shares and likes to redirect traffic; fabricating user activity to make certain content appear more popular; comment section abuse by posting false information; and using malicious tags or keywords to boost search rankings for specific content.
R0024.influence: Malicious traffic diversion through user-generated content may lead to fake traffic, economic losses, decreased user trust, brand reputation damage, and negative impacts on community health.

observables: Comments and direct messages embed traffic-diversion contact details such as WeChat IDs, QQ numbers, or external links
A single account batch-posts near-duplicate diversion scripts across multiple target content items
External redirect links clicked from diversion content point to high-risk or grey-market sites
Newly registered accounts, after a warming-up period, burst into diversion content with mechanical timing
Diversion accounts cluster with SIM-bank cards and device-control fingerprints, with highly homogeneous IP ranges
